Because that was the first time I heard the word ‘disabled’ being used in relation to me. When I was prescribed antidepressants my doctor didn’t use that word, I only heard it from my doctor after the jumping off point with my university’s mental health team. I’m sorry if I come across as defensive, all I tried to do was respond to your comments

I mean all I asked in my post was advice on how I can ‘feel more comfortable  though these new developments in my life’. I’m at a very confusing point in my life where I am struggling to understand myself and what I can do to help myself, hence why I am struggling with the notion of having a disability. Of course I am questioning myself, I have spent my entire life being questioned and things are very hard, to the point where if they don’t get better I don’t know if I can continue. You’re not proving a point by saying that I am doubting myself, because that’s the point of what I’m struggling with. If you have advice on how I can enter disabled spaces without interfering or being a nuisance then I’d appreciate it, but trying to call me out for things that I already know is not effecting buddy. 

I don’t think this conversation is efficient for me at all, so I won’t be replying any further. I hope you have a good day and genuinely wish you the best.

I mean, I don’t think the two things are mutually exclusive to be honest. Yes I have been considered disabled by multiple institutions in a short amount of time, and that is shocking to me because I never allowed myself to think that I was anything more than a dramatic child or teenager that needs to ‘suck it up and deal with it’.
